calls.reason: Two incidents before the post exist: Lemkin's Replit deletion, later restored, and a Cursor forum allegation. Nothing shows reports every day or two, and Replit's account points to dev/production setup, not simply LLM unreliability.

METR found 40% allowed unrestricted command execution on low-stakes projects, and 1Password found persistent agent access. Neither shows the access was excessive or driven by convenience; the GitHub issue is one user.

Before the post, Pillar Security (rule files) and Invariant Labs (public GitHub issues) showed malicious content in agent context causing unauthorized actions. That fits the plain reading that injected content can cause trouble.

The IDEsaster studies found new attack paths after nearly 30 patches across 12 vendors. That fits the claim, but there is no deadline and no evidence of real attacks going unstopped, so the open-ended forecast can't be settled.
